hook: Forensic chemists can tell which pen wrote a note by separating the dyes in its ink. Refineries split crude oil into gasoline and diesel. Each separation works because the parts of a mixture are held by different forces.

prereq.q: Which liquid has the higher vapor pressure at 25 °C?
options: The one with weaker intermolecular forces
The one with stronger intermolecular forces
prereq.why: Weaker attractions let more molecules escape.

prereq.q: Which molecule can hydrogen-bond to an –OH group?
prereq.why: Methanol has an O–H group and lone pairs on O.

figure.caption: Rf compares how far each spot traveled with how far the solvent traveled.

chain.cause: Components of a mixture differ in size, attractions or volatility
chain.effect: physical methods can separate them without changing them

chain.cause: In chromatography each component is pulled by a stationary and a mobile phase
chain.effect: the one held more by the stationary phase moves more slowly and has a smaller Rf

chain.cause: In distillation the component with weaker intermolecular forces has the higher vapor pressure
chain.effect: it boils off first and is collected first

chain.cause: Undissolved solids are larger than filter pores; dissolved particles are not
chain.effect: filtration removes solids but cannot separate a solution

ideas: Filtration: undissolved solid from liquid, by size.
Chromatography: stronger attraction to the stationary phase means slower movement. Rf = spot distance ÷ solvent distance.
Paper is polar: polar components lag; a more polar solvent carries them farther.
Distillation: weaker intermolecular forces, higher vapor pressure, vaporizes first.

misconception.wrong: In chromatography, heavier molecules move more slowly because they are harder to carry.
misconception.right: Separation follows attractions, not mass. A component held more strongly by the stationary phase moves more slowly, whatever its mass.

summary: Mixtures are separated by physical properties that trace back to particle forces. Filtration removes undissolved solids by size. Chromatography separates components by their attraction to a stationary phase versus a mobile phase, measured by Rf. Distillation separates liquids by vapor pressure: weaker intermolecular forces vaporize first.
